Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:10:1.english: His tradition - [Refers to the clause:] "But they said" ([according to which] he holds in accordance with Ze’eiri).

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:10:2.english: His reasoning - "But I myself do not say so, etc."

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:11:1.english: Where it discharged at the end of six [months] - That we saw that it began to discharge at the beginning of the seventh month.

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:11:2.hebrew: אין טינוף פחות מל' יום - דאינה מקבלת זכר עד ל' יום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:11:2.english: A murky discharge is no less than thirty days - For it does not accept a male until thirty days [have passed].

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:12:1.hebrew: לגמריה - דלא ידעינן שטינפה בת ששה, אדר' ישמעאל פליג, דאמר: בת שנתה ודאי לכהן, וקא"ל איהו: אפילו ילדה בתוך שנתה — ספק, דלמא טניף בתוך ג' חדשים או ד' משנולדה, וחזרה וילדה בתוך שנתה. והיכא דחזינן דלא טניף עד סוף ששה, וטינפה בסוף ששה כדאמר רבי יהושע בסבריה — ההוא בכור מעליא הוא, דההוא טינוף לאו טינוף גמור הוא, דאם טינוף היה, לא הוה ילדה בתוך שנתה עד יום אחד בשנה שניה; דטינוף הוי כל חדש שביעי כזעירי, וה' חדשים ימי העיבור — הרי כלתה שנתה, ולא תלד עד למחר, דכל חדשי עיבור בעינן שלמים, ואחר כך יולדת למחר; כדאמרינן במסכת נדה (דף לח:): "ויתן ה' לה הריון" — בגימט' רע"א, וט' חדשים של ל' יום הוו ר"ע ימים, וביום רע"א כתב קרא דיולדת:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:12:1.english: According to his tradition - Where we do not know that it discharged at six months, he disagrees with Rabbi Yishmael, who says: [If an animal gives birth] within its year, [the offspring] definitely [belongs] to the priest; and he says to him: Even if it gave birth within its year, it is in doubt, lest it discharged within three or four months from when it was born, and then became pregnant again and gave birth within its year. But where we saw that it did not discharge until the end of six [months], and it discharged at the end of six [months], as Rabbi Yehoshua stated according to his own reasoning — that is a full-fledged firstborn, because that discharge was not a valid discharge; for if it had been a [valid] discharge, it would not have given birth within its year until one day into the second year. For a discharge lasts all through the seventh month, in accordance with Ze’eiri, and five months are the days of gestation — behold, its year has ended, and it will not give birth until the following day, for we require all months of gestation to be complete, and only afterward does it give birth on the following day; as we say in tractate Niddah (38b): “And the Lord gave her conception” (Ruth 4:13) — [herayon] in gematria is 271, and nine months of thirty days are 270 days, and on the 271st day Scripture writes that she gives birth.

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:12:2.hebrew: לסבריה - ואף על גב דחזינא דלא טניף עד סוף ששה, נמי ספיקא הוא, דלית ליה דזעירי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:12:2.english: According to his [own] reasoning - Even though we saw that it did not discharge until the end of six [months], it is also [a matter of] doubt, because he does not accept [the statement] of Ze’eiri.

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:2:1.hebrew: רובא דתלי במעשה - כגון עיבור הבהמה, דתלי בהרבעה, ואיכא למיחש שמא לא עלה עליה זכר. הילכך, ספק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:2:1.english: A majority that is dependent upon an action - Such as the pregnancy of an animal, which depends on mating, and there is reason to be concerned that perhaps a male did not mount her. Therefore, [its status is in] doubt:

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:5:1.english: And I do not say so - I do not dispute you with the wording of my received tradition, but rather with a different wording. And later, [the Gemara] explains what [difference] there is between his reasoning and his tradition.

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:6:1.hebrew: במאי קמיפלגי ר' ישמעאל - וגמריה דר' יהושע, דקתני אבל אמרו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:6:1.english: With regard to what do Rabbi Yishmael [and Rabbi Yehoshua] disagree - [That is, Rabbi Yishmael] and the tradition of Rabbi Yehoshua, which taught: “However, they said.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:6:2.hebrew: בטינוף פוטר פליגי - דרבי ישמעאל, דמשוי ליה ודאי בכור, סבר: דאי נמי טניף בתוך שנתה — לא מיפטרא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:6:2.english: They disagree [over whether] a murky discharge exempts - For Rabbi Yishmael, who treats it as a definite firstborn, holds that even if it had a discharge within its [first] year, it is not exempted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:8:1.hebrew: לחומרא - כגון גבי רישא דשמעתא, דאי הוה אזלינן בתר רובא, הוה משוינן ליה פשוט ודאי, (דהא) מכאן ואילך (הוה). הילכך, חייש למיעוט לחומרא, ומשוי ליה ספק. אבל הכא, אי חייש למיעוט — קולא הוא, דאפילו בת שנתה משוי ליה ספק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 20a:8:1.english: To a stringency - For example, regarding the beginning of the discussion, where if we were to follow the majority, we would render it definitely ordinary, (as) [the case of] “from that point forward” (was). Therefore, he is concerned for the minority as a stringency and renders it an uncertain [firstborn]. But here, if he were concerned for the minority, it would be a leniency, as he would render even [the offspring of an animal] within its first year an uncertain [firstborn].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:1:1.hebrew: מחוורתא רבי ישמעאל כר"מ ס"ל דחייש למיעוטא - ומטעם סמוך מיעוטא דאין מתעברות לחזקה דבחזקת שלא ילדה ואיתרע ליה רובא, אין לחושבו ודאי בכור, דלא הוי אלא פלגא ופלגא, כדאמר בר"פ בתרא דיבמות (דף קיט.), ושם הארכתי. והא דמטהרינן בספק טומאה בפרק כסוי הדם (חולין דף פו.) — היינו משום דילפינן מסוטה ליטהר בדבר שאין בו דעת לישאל; ולהכי קאמר התם: אם אמרו ספק טומאה לטהר, יאמרו ספק איסור להיתר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:1:1.english: “It is clear that Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for the minority” - And on account of [the principle]: “Join the minority [of animals] that do not become pregnant to the presumption, as [the animal is] in the presumption of not having given birth, and the majority is impaired” — one cannot consider it a certain firstborn, for it is only [rendered] half-and-half, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of the last chapter of Yevamot (119a), and there I elaborated. And as for that which we rule pure in [a case of] doubtful ritual impurity in the chapter [entitled] Kisui HaDam (Chullin 86a) — that is because we derive from [the case of a] sotah to rule pure regarding a matter that lacks understanding to be questioned; and for that reason [the Gemara] says there: “If they said [so regarding] doubtful ritual impurity, to rule pure, will they say [so regarding] a doubtful prohibition, to permit?”

Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:2:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר אפילו תימא רבנן - תימה: דלא משני הכי בר"פ בתרא דיבמות (דף קיט. ושם) אמתני', דלא תנשא ולא תתייבם עד שתדע שמא [מעוברת] היא צרתה. וי"ל: דתשמיש דאדם לא חשיב תלי במעשה כמו תשמיש דבהמה — דפעמים דבהמה צריך להרביע, כדאמר בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף צא.): מותר להכניס כמכחול בשפופרת:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:2:1.english: Ravina says: You may even say [in accordance with] the Rabbis - It is puzzling that [the Gemara] does not answer this [way] at the beginning of the last chapter of Yevamot (119a, and see there) regarding the Mishnah [which states]: "She may neither marry nor enter into levirate marriage until she knows whether her co-wife is [pregnant]." And one can say that human intercourse is not considered dependent upon an action like the mating of animals, for at times an animal needs to be mated [by a person], as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaSokher Et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 91a): "It is permitted to insert [the male organ] like a brush into a tube."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:7:1.hebrew: ורבי יהושע סבר חוששין לטינוף - וא"ת: הא קא מסקינן לקמן דרבי יהושע לא חייש למיעוטא, כדדייק ממתני': "דיצתה מלאה, ר' יהושע אומר: אינה חוששת", וא"כ היכי חייש הכא למיעוטא דמטנפות? ועוד, דבכי האי גוונא דהכא אפילו ר"מ לא חייש, כדאמר בריש פרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קיט:): דהיכא דאיכא רובא וחזקה, הוי המיעוט מיעוט דמיעוטא; והכא איכא רובא דאין מטנפות, וחזקה שהיא בחזקת שלא ילדה! וי"ל, דמ"מ לא הוי ודאי בכור שניתן לכהן, דאיכא חזקת ממונא דעדיפא, והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה. ואפילו לרב, דאזיל בממונא אחר הרוב בההיא דהמוכר שור לחבירו ונמצא נגחן (ב"ק דף מו.) — היינו משום דאמר: "קים לי בנפשאי שאני מן הרוב"; א"נ, יש לחלק בין ממון שאין לו תובעין לממון שיש לו תובעין. ומיהו היא קצת תימה: דלענין ללקות בגיזה ועבודה ולענין ליקרב למזבח חשיב ודאי בכור, דאזלינן בתר רובא וחזקה, ולענין נתינתו לכהן יחשב ספק?! ונראה לתרץ, דלהכי חיישינן למיעוט דמטנפות, משום דרוב בהמות מתעברות כשמגיעות לזמן שראויות להתעבר בו (מתעברות):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:7:1.english: "And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that one is concerned about a murky discharge" - And if you say: But we conclude later that Rabbi Yehoshua is not concerned for a minority, as [the Gemara] deduces from the Mishnah: "If [an animal] went out full, Rabbi Yehoshua says: She is not suspect" — and if so, how is he concerned here for the minority [of animals] that expel a murky discharge? And furthermore, in a case such as this here, even Rabbi Meir is not concerned, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of the last chapter of Yevamot (119b): that wherever there is a majority and a presumption, the minority is [considered] a minority of a minority; and here there is a majority [of animals] that do not expel a murky discharge, and a presumption that it has the status of not having given birth! And one can say that nevertheless, it is not a definite firstborn that must be given to a priest, as there is the presumption of monetary possession, which is superior, and "he who extracts from his fellow bears the burden of proof." And even according to Rav, who follows the majority in monetary matters in that case of "one who sells an ox to his fellow and it is found to be a goring ox" (Bava Kamma 46a) — that is because [the buyer] says: "It is established to myself that I am of the majority"; alternatively, one can distinguish between money that has no [specific] claimants and money that has claimants. However, this is somewhat astonishing: that regarding [incurring] lashes for shearing and labor, and regarding being sacrificed upon the Altar, it would be considered a definite firstborn, as we follow the majority and the presumption, yet regarding giving it to the priest it would be considered an uncertainty?! And it seems [preferable] to answer that this is why we are concerned for the minority that expel a murky discharge: because most animals become pregnant when they reach the time at which they are fit to become pregnant (become pregnant).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:8:1.hebrew: לקולא לא חייש - ואפילו לכהן ינתן, כיון דקרב למזבח. ומיהו גבי חמורה קשה: דהוה לן להעמיד ממון ביד בעלים ולא ניזל בתר רובא, דאפילו רב מודה הכא דאין הולכין בממון אחר הרוב, כדפי' לעיל. וי"ל: דגזר חמורה אטו בהמה טהורה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:8:1.english: "He is not concerned for a leniency" - And [the offspring] is given even to the priest, since it is offered on the altar. However, regarding a female donkey it is difficult, for we should leave the money in the possession of the owner and not follow the majority, for even Rav concedes here that we do not follow the majority in monetary matters, as we explained above. And one can say that [Rabbi Yishmael] decreed [the case of] a female donkey on account of a kosher animal.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:9:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא בין לקולא בין לחומרא חייש - מעיקרא נמי דהוה בעי למימר: "לקולא לא חייש", משמע דהיינו לר' ישמעאל, אבל לר"מ בכ"מ חייש. ומכ"מ אין לדקדק מכאן דהא דר"מ חייש למיעוטא היינו מדאורייתא, מדחייש הכא אפילו להקל — דהיינו שלא נותנו לכהן — דלא אזלינן בממון אחר הרוב; א"נ, משום דאיכא רוב מתעברות כשמגיעות לזמן הראויות להתעבר, שמסייע למיעוט. ובפ' אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף לד:) גבי גבינת בית אונייקי אמר: דר"מ חייש למיעוטא, וגזר רובא אטו מיעוטא, ולא גזר שאר מקומות אטו אותו מקום — משמע דבאותו מקום נמי לאו מדאורייתא, אלא מדרבנן, מטעם גזירה אטו מיעוטא. ובפ"ק דחולין (דף יב.) נמי, דפריך לר"מ: "פסח וקדשים מאי איכא למימר דשרא רחמנא?" ולא קאמר: "בשר תאוה מאי איכא למימר דשרא רחמנא?" — משמע דמדרבנן חייש למיעוטא; ואפילו גזר בבשר תאוה, בפסח וקדשים לא גזר דלא אפשר, ואף על פי שלא יכלו להעמיד שם גזירתם, העמידוה היכא דאפשר. ה"נ בדאורייתא: היכא דאפשר — אפשר, היכא דלא אפשר לבדוק — לא אפשר; דאם איתא דבדאורייתא אין חילוק בין אפשר ללא אפשר, לא היה לחכמים לחוש ולגזור היכא דאפשר, כיון שראו שום מקום שלא חשו, כגון היכא דלא אפשר. ומיהו, היכא דחזקה מסייעת למיעוט, נראה דחייש ר"מ למיעוט מדאורייתא, מדטהר גבי תינוק; ועוד, רוצה להתיר בפרק כיסוי הדם (חולין דף פו:) לשחוט אותו ואת בנו אחר שחיטת חרש, שוטה וקטן, דאף על גב דאין רוב מעשיהן מקולקלין. וא"ת: דבפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף נה:) גבי חמשה חומשין הן, משמע דדמאי הוי מדרבנן אפילו לר"מ, דקאמר: "עשו חיזוק לדבריהם", ולמה אינו טבל דאורייתא, דסמוך מיעוט דאין מעשרים לחזקת טבל? וי"ל: דאין זה חזקה, דדלמא כרבי אושעיא עבדה, שהכניסה במוץ (ברכות דף לא.); ועוד, דאין להחזיק שום אדם ברשע בשביל מיעוט שאין מעשרין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 20a:9:1.english: And if you wish, say [instead]: Whether [it leads] to a leniency or whether to a stringency, he is concerned - Initially as well, when [the Gemara] sought to say that he is not concerned [for a minority] where it leads to a leniency, it implied that this was [only] according to Rabbi Yishmael, whereas according to Rabbi Meir, he is concerned in every case. And nevertheless, one cannot deduce from here that this [principle] of Rabbi Meir that he is concerned for a minority is from the Torah, from [the fact] that he is concerned here even to be lenient — namely, that we do not give it to the priest — because in monetary matters we do not follow the majority; alternatively, because there is a majority [of animals that] conceive when they reach the time when they are fit to conceive, which supports the minority [that expelled a discharge]. And in the chapter [entitled] "Ein Ma'amidin" (Avodah Zarah 34b) regarding the cheese of Beit Oniyki, [the Gemara] said: Rabbi Meir is concerned for the minority, and decreed [against consuming the cheese of the] majority on account of the minority, but did not decree other places on account of that place — which implies that even in that place [its prohibition] is not from the Torah, but rather by Rabbinic law, by reason of a decree on account of the minority. And also in the first chapter of Chullin (12a), where [the Gemara] objects to Rabbi Meir: "With regard to the Paschal offering and consecrated offerings, what is there to say, since the Merciful One permitted [them]?" and it does not say: "With regard to meat of desire [ordinary meat], what is there to say, since the Merciful One permitted [it]?" — this implies that [only] by Rabbinic law is he concerned for the minority; and even though they decreed regarding meat of desire, regarding the Paschal offering and consecrated offerings they did not decree because it is not possible [to inspect], and even though they could not maintain their decree there, they maintained it wherever possible. So too with regard to Torah law: Where it is possible [to inspect] — it is possible; where it is not possible to inspect — it is not possible. For if it were so that by Torah law there is no distinction between [where it is] possible and [where it is] not possible, the Sages would not have been concerned and decreed [to follow the minority] where it is possible, since they saw a certain place where [the Torah] was not concerned, such as where it is not possible. However, where a presumption [chazakah] supports the minority, it appears that Rabbi Meir is concerned for the minority by Torah law, since he ruled [the mother] pure in the case of a child; and furthermore, he wishes to permit in the chapter [entitled] "Kisui HaDam" (Chullin 86b) to slaughter "it and its offspring" [on the same day] after the slaughter performed by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, even though a majority of their actions are not flawed. And if you say: In the chapter [entitled] "HaZahav" (Bava Metzia 55b) regarding "There are five fifths," it implies that demai [doubtfully tithed produce] is [forbidden only] by Rabbinic law even according to Rabbi Meir, as [the Gemara] says: "They reinforced their words" — but why is it not tevel [untithed produce] by Torah law, for let us join the minority who do not tithe to the presumption of tevel? And one can say: This is not a [valid] presumption, for perhaps [the owner] acted in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Oshaya, where he brought it in [to the house] while in its chaff (Berakhot 31a) [so that the obligation to tithe never took effect]; and furthermore, one does not presume any person to be wicked on account of a minority who do not tithe.
